pathMatrix.reason: DECIDED, not merely open. `P1-27-OD-005` (`open-decisions.md:795-978`, recorded by `c060b93`) ships last-writer-wins on every CRM and Vehicle write: no route under `customers/`, `customer-duplicates/`, `vehicles/` or `vehicle-duplicates/` declares `versionGuarded: true`, and none reads `expectedVersion`, so an `If-Match` sent from here would be parsed and discarded. There is no stale-version path to exercise, and the plan's §4 forbids creating one from this branch. The decision names the Backend remediation that would create it, and six executable checks in `api-client.test.ts:1242-1337` fail the day it lands — which is what stops this row ageing into a lie. The status stays `ABSENT` because a path that cannot be exercised is not a path that has been proved; what changed is that the absence is now ratified rather than unacknowledged. The case cited records the absence.

pathMatrix.reason: The same ratified decision, `P1-27-OD-005`. Concurrent edits are last-writer-wins from a client position — the `ERR-CON-001` the services do raise guards a version the service itself read inside its own transaction (`vehicle-write-service.ts:115` to `:132`), so it catches a writer landing inside the server's SELECT-to-UPDATE window and cannot catch a lost update across an operator's read-edit-submit cycle. `A42-13` records the finding and it still holds; `P1-27-OD-005` disposes of it. `ABSENT` for the same reason as the row above.

pathMatrix.reason: Stronger than it was, and still not the whole path. That a key is sent on every write and on no read is proven, and since `c060b93` it is proven over a set DERIVED from the adapters (23 writes, against 11 written by hand) and read off the wire from a request a shipped adapter produced, rather than from a pure function. What is still absent is the replay itself: no case issues the same P1-27 request twice and counts the server-side effects as a delta. That is a server property, and the two places it IS proved do not reach a P1-27 operation — `tests/backend/idempotency.test.ts` proves the MECHANISM with effects counted but over a generic command, and `tests/backend/p1-14-idempotency-replay.test.ts` proves it per-operation for IAM and for no CRM or Vehicle operation. Both are cited so the gap is bounded rather than open-ended.

weakCitations.what: Citations that resolve to an executable case which does not prove the behaviour the id names.
weakCitations.why: Five of the twenty-nine were spot-checked by an independent reader and two of them resolved to an assertion that two CONSTANTS differ. That is a real case and it is not a proof: it would pass against a screen that ignored both constants. "29 resolve" is therefore not "29 proved", and this block exists so the headline cannot be read as the stronger claim. Each entry keeps the weak citation rather than deleting it — deleting evidence to improve a record is the defect one level up — and names the case that now carries the obligation.
weakCitations.checkedBy: scripts/ci/check-p1-27-doc-counts.mjs (checkCatalogue): every entry must name a recorded id, a file that exists, a case title present in that file, a stated weakness, and a strengthening proof whose titles resolve too.
